metadata.case_name: CHEUNG KA LOK v. MAU WA CONSTRUCTION LTD AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.expected_occupation_after: security guard or petrol station attendant

manifestations.description: Limited movement of the right knee; inability to squat; difficulty climbing stairs
Swelling over the right knee with tenderness
Wasting and marked atrophy in his right quadriceps; thigh girth at 10cm above the patella of his right leg was 1.5 to 2cm less than his left thigh
Intermittent low back pain, localized to the midline and right side of his low back; mechanical in nature; pain aggravated by walking, stairs, slopes and toilet use
Left foot numbness and both lower limb pain
Lower limb power of grade 4 out of 5 bilaterally on L2 and L3 myotomes (reduced lower limb power)
Difficulty lifting objects (capacity reported up to 5kg); reduced right knee extension strength (about half of left); difficulty deep squatting
Depressed mood, irritability, sense of uselessness, pain fear, negative thoughts, sense of helplessness and loss of control, intense anger, fleeting suicidal ideas
Occasional auditory hallucinations / vague pseudo-hallucinations (imaginary noises and voices calling his name)
Problems with sleep and appetite; difficulty accepting life changes and chronic pain; social withdrawal with few social contacts

treatments_received: Accident & Emergency Department assessment and treatment
X-ray examinations (chest, left ribs, right knee)
Physiotherapy (first course: 20 July 2011 to 3 April 2012; 41 sessions; second course: 6 December 2012 to 10 January 2013; 5 sessions)
Occupational therapy and work rehabilitation (including lifting and functional capacity training)
Supportive psychotherapy and coaching of emotional regulation skills
8-day intensive Multidisciplinary Approach to Chronic Pain Rehabilitation Program (20 August 2012 to 28 September 2012)
Admission to psychiatric ward (4 October 2013 to 10 October 2013)
treatments_future: private psychiatric treatment (10 sessions) - as provided for in award

losses.description: Reduced function of right knee due to partial tears of medial collateral ligament and probable anterior cruciate ligament and residual lower back soft tissue injury resulting in intermittent pain and reduced physical capacity

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: Unable to manage certain tasks such as changing a light bulb due to pain and reduced mobility
Deterioration of relationship with his wife leading to divorce attributed to psychological and psychosocial consequences of the accident
Inability to continue work as a construction site labourer and reduced earning capacity; required to seek light duties such as security guard or petrol station attendant

Both experts agreed that the plaintiff had suffered some soft tissue injury to his back. He suffered a contusion injury to his back and has had psychiatric symptoms. He was diagnosed with adjustment disorder and was given an anti-depressant. Dr Law's opinion was that the plaintiff suffered adjustment disorder with depressed mood wholly caused by the accident and consistent with the injury. His diagnosis was revised from adjustment disorder to psychotic depression with anti-psychotics offered.
